instructions: Fill in the correct form of the possessive article.

items.explanation: Bruder is masculine, and in the nominative mein takes no ending, just like ein Bruder.
Schwester is feminine, so mein takes -e, just like eine Schwester.
Auto is neuter, and in the nominative dein has no ending, like ein Auto.
Tasche is feminine, so dein takes -e: deine Tasche.
The father is male, so sein-; Familie is feminine (accusative = nominative), so it takes -e: seine Familie.
Frau Klein is a woman, so her = ihr-; Mutter is feminine, so it takes -e: ihre Mutter.
Vater is the masculine accusative object of fragen, so mein takes -en, just like einen Vater.
Bruder is the masculine object (accusative), so dein becomes deinen.
Opa is a masculine accusative object, so unser takes -en: unseren Opa, like einen Opa.
Haus is neuter in the nominative, so unser has no ending, like ein Haus.
Mutter is feminine, so dein takes -e: deine Mutter.

items.prompt: Guten Tag! Wie ist ___ Name, bitte?
items.explanation: Name is masculine nominative, so no ending. The formal Sie form is written Ihr with a capital I.
In the plural nominative the possessive takes -e: unsere Kinder (like keine Kinder).

items.prompt: Das ist das Haus von Tom und Lisa. Dort ist ___ Garten.
items.explanation: ihr (their) refers to Tom and Lisa; Garten is masculine nominative, so no ending.
Ball is a masculine accusative object, so euer takes -en (and drops the e): euren Ball.
Fahrrad is neuter nominative, so euer has no ending, like ein Fahrrad.
Handy is neuter, and in the accusative neuter has no ending, like ein Handy.
Neuter accusative equals nominative: no ending, like ein Buch.
Brille is feminine, and the accusative feminine takes -e: meine Brille.

items.prompt: Herr Braun, haben Sie ___ Ausweis dabei?
items.explanation: Ausweis is a masculine accusative object, so the formal Ihr takes -en: Ihren Ausweis.
Eltern is plural, and the plural takes -e in the accusative: meine Eltern.

items.prompt: Das ist Tom und das ist ___ Schwester.
items.explanation: er becomes sein-; Schwester is feminine, so it takes -e: seine Schwester.
sie (Frau Schulz) becomes ihr-; Bruder is masculine accusative, so it takes -en: ihren Bruder.
du becomes dein-; Jacke is feminine, so it takes -e: deine Jacke.
wir becomes unser-; masculine accusative takes -en: unseren Hund.
Plural nouns take -e after the possessive: deine Schuhe.
The formal Sie gives Ihr- with a capital I; Tasche is feminine, so Ihre Tasche.
Schirm is masculine accusative, so mein takes -en: meinen Schirm.
ihr becomes euer; Gemüse is neuter accusative, so no ending: euer Gemüse.
für takes the accusative; plural Freunde takes -e: seine Freunde.
